title: Investigation of perovskite related oxides: structural and magnetic properties
abstract: Perovskites exist in varied structures and show structure dependent magnetic properties which is of great interest in the field of multiferroics, magnetocaloric and spintronic devices. Here we intend to study the various rare-earth(R) and transition metal (TM) ion interactions depending on their structures. Different Curie temperature, spinglass transition and spin reorientation transitions were observed depending on the degree of interactions and structural properties. It is interesting to study the role of orbital interactions, disorder in magnetic transitions leading to change in superexchange and double exchange interaction. On substitution at A-site or B-site results in change in magnetic interactions, as well as creates structural distortions. We also obtained results where the spin interaction of the transition metal and rare-earth interaction, magnetic anisotropy, orientations of orbitals, disorder induced interactions were observed.
summary: This work systematically investigates the structural and magnetic properties of various perovskite oxides, focusing on how substituting rare-earth and transition metal ions influences magnetic interactions. By combining structural and magnetic measurements, the authors demonstrate that phenomena like spin reorientation and magnetic ordering are critically dependent on lattice distortions and competing exchange mechanisms.
main_problem: The study investigates the structure-dependent magnetic properties of perovskite-related oxides, which are crucial for multiferroics, magnetocaloric, and spintronic applications.
main_result: The magnetic behavior, including Curie temperatures, spin-glass transitions, and spin reorientations, is highly sensitive to structural distortions, rare-earth ion size, and the interplay between superexchange and double exchange interactions.
method: The research employs a combination of structural characterization (PXRD, XPS, EDAX) and magnetic measurements (magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization) across various substituted perovskite compositions.
model_or_system: The physical systems are perovskite oxides ($	ext{ABO}_3$) incorporating rare-earth (R) and transition metal (TM) ions (e.g., $	ext{R}_x	ext{Sr}_{1-x}	ext{Fe}_{0.5}	ext{Mn}_{0.5}	ext{O}_3$). The complexity arises from the interplay between orbital interactions, structural distortions (like octahedral tilting), and competing magnetic exchange mechanisms.
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$ vs T), magnetic hysteresis ($M$ vs $H$), transition temperatures ($T_C, T_N, T_S$), lattice parameters ($a, b, c$), and bond angles.
important_parameters: Rare-earth ion size/substitution ($x$), temperature (T), applied magnetic field (H), and the degree of structural distortion.
main_assumptions: The magnetic properties are assumed to be governed by superexchange and double exchange interactions modulated by crystal structure.
figures_summary: The notes reference multiple figures showing magnetic susceptibility vs. temperature, magnetization vs. field, and structural parameter changes across different compositions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates several specific perovskite systems (e.g., $	ext{Ho-Pr-Mn-Cr-O}$, $	ext{R-Sr-Fe-Mn-O}$) using a suite of characterization techniques, culminating in a comparative summary table of structural and magnetic data.
why_interesting: The detailed study of magnetic transitions, spin reorientation, and the role of orbital interactions in perovskites provides rich material for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated materials.
